purpose.description: Construct explicit counterexamples showing how nonstationary drift breaks previously valid factorization.
purpose.role: Identify failure boundaries between stationary and evolving interface sufficiency.
not_used_for: assuming historical data always becomes obsolete
equating distribution shift with target failure

failure_condition.statement: There exist systems f_a, f_b where observations are equivalent under the interface but targets diverge over time.

counterexamples.name: hidden_transition_change
counterexamples.description: Two systems begin with identical dynamics but gradually diverge in transition behavior.

counterexamples.name: regime_transition_alias
counterexamples.description: Different hidden regimes produce identical observations immediately before a transition.

counterexamples.name: adaptive_lag_failure
counterexamples.description: The environment changes faster than the interface can update.

counterexamples.name: history_misleading
counterexamples.description: Past observations preserve the wrong equivalence structure after a gradual system change.

shared_pattern.statement: A previously sufficient interface becomes insufficient when drift changes target-relevant equivalence classes.

theoretical_implication.finding: Nonstationarity does not invalidate factorization; it invalidates fixed interfaces whose equivalence classes no longer match the target.

decision.meaning: Drift counterexamples establish the boundary where static interfaces fail under changing system structure.

notes: The failure is not caused by change alone but by change that modifies target-relevant distinctions.
Historical information can become actively misleading after regime change.
Adaptive interfaces preserve factorization by tracking evolving observation boundaries.
